legacyPolicy: Exact known original first-five root links, marked or unmarked, open current practice with a disclosure. /archive preserves literal settings and historical replay. Custom and nonstandard counting links remain literal.

mapping.purpose: Supported application: eight different four-beat quarter/pair bars, not twelve alternating one-beat prompts.
mapping.preparation: Teach four numbered quarter-note beats and the number/& response lesson first. The short one-beat introduction and two-beat practice remain available as warm-ups.

mapping.purpose: Supported integration of already prepared quarter/pair cells and eighth-rest order over a full bar. Eight notation arrangements give seven distinct count patterns.
mapping.preparation: Teach eighth-note/rest order using the inline examples and Notes & Rests before this application. Different written durations can share a count.

mapping.purpose: A brief reduced-support recognition sample of the same prepared four-beat rest vocabulary. Multiple choice, previous practice and possible pool overlap remain supports; this is not independent mastery.
mapping.preparation: Complete supported mixed-rest bars first. Guide off, feedback at the end, retry button off; reopening remains possible.

mapping.purpose: Supported meter transfer: six of eight quarter/pair bars in 3/4. Restore the guide and use familiar note values while learning a different bar length.
mapping.preparation: Teach three quarter-note beats per 3/4 bar and restarting at 1. This is not a harder notation pool. Use the optional two-beat practice if changing bar length is new.

mapping.purpose: A short notation/response introduction: all five target one-beat patterns once each. Small pools and deliberate replay are appropriate here; twelve responses are unnecessary.
mapping.preparation: Divide one quarter-note beat into four equal positions: 1 e & a. Four sixteenth notes start at all four positions. A sixteenth rest, one sixteenth note, then an eighth rest starts only on e. An eighth rest, a sixteenth rest, then one sixteenth note starts only on a. Alternating sixteenth rests and notes start on e and a. A sixteenth rest, two sixteenth notes, then a sixteenth rest starts on e and &. Rests take time but have no note start. This fragment starts on beat 1; 2 in a wrong choice is a wrong beat number, not another beat here. Read supplied choices as note starts. Five questions introduce these five patterns once each; replay them deliberately if helpful, then try the separate supported bar application when ready.
